```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(codehover)
```

# Automatic code hover

Write your ggplot inside `ch_hover({ ... })`. The code is split at every
top-level `+`, one image is rendered per step, and the hoverable table is
returned ready to use — CSS and JavaScript are attached automatically.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
ch_hover({
  ggplot(cars, aes(x = speed, y = dist)) +
    geom_point(color = "red") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(title = "A ggplot for the rest of us",
         subtitle = "Hover each row to see that step") +
    theme_bw()
}, width = 4, height = 3)
```

# Keeping the source clean

Alternatively, write the plot in a normal chunk with `eval=FALSE` and
reference it by label, so your document shows the plain code:

```{r myplot, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
ggplot(cars, aes(x = speed, y = dist)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```

`r ch_hover_chunk("myplot", width = 4, height = 3)`

# Useful options

* `layout = "auto"` (default) places the image beside the code when there
  is room and below it otherwise; `"row"` forces side by side, `"column"`
  forces the image below.
* `type = "one_row"` highlights only the hovered row (default is incremental).
* `fixed_scales = TRUE` pins axes and legends from the final plot so the
  image does not jump between steps.
* `path = "assets/"` keeps the step PNGs on disk instead of embedding them
  as base64 (smaller HTML file).
